results.content: With less than two weeks to go before the congressional elections, Americans are nearly as gloomy about the economy as they were when the nation was emerging from the pandemic, and President Donald Trump's economic approval rating is hitting an all-time low, according to the latest CNBC All-America Economic Survey. Overall, 63% of the public is pessimistic about the current state of the economy and the outlook, up 1 percentage point from the July survey. But that percentage now includes 35% of Republicans, up 6 points from July and the highest level of Republican pessimism of either of Trump's two terms. Most registered voters disapprove of Donald Trump's job performance, as has been the case for months: 40% strongly or somewhat approve of how Trump is handling his job, while 59% disapprove.

results.content: This Democratic lead in the 2026 U.S. House elections comes amid President Donald Trump's continued unpopularity. 34% of U.S. adult citizens strongly or somewhat approve of Trump's job handling, and 62% disapprove — a net job approval of -28. That's in line with recent weeks but down from a year ago, when Trump's net approval was regularly between -10 and -20. It's also far lower than Trump's net job approval at this point in his first term (-10) or Joe Biden's at this point in his term (-1).

Taylor Orth-October 14, 2026

The latest Economist / YouGov Poll finds that roughly half (49%) of Americans say the current state of the American economy is poor, the largest share since July 2022. Only 20% describe the economy as excellent (4%) or good (16%).
